steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: On 27 February 1933, the Reichstag building in Berlin was set on fire. Marinus van der Lubbe, a Dutch Communist, was found at the scene and arrested. Hitler used the fire to persuade Hindenburg to issue the Decree for the Protection of the People and State on 28 February 1933, which suspended all civil liberties. | Key Fact: In the March 1933 election, the Nazis won 43.9% of the vote (288 seats). This was not a majority, but combined with the DNVP's 8% (52 seats), Hitler had a majority in the Reichstag. The election was held in an atmosphere of terror - SA thugs patrolled the streets, opposition meetings were banned, and the Communist Party was effectively illegal. | Key Fact: The Enabling Act (Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Reich), passed on 23 March 1933, gave

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how the Reichstag Fire helped Hitler consolidate power. (4 marks) | How important was the Enabling Act in the establishment of the Nazi dictatorship? (8 marks) | "The Night of the Long Knives was the most important event in Hitler's consolidation of power." How far do you agree? (12 marks)
